differentials.name: Stable angina pectoris
differentials.not_most_likely_because: The 2021 AHA/ACC Chest Pain Guideline draws the acute/stable line on CHANGE, not on whether pain occurs at rest: 'stable' is reserved for symptoms that are chronic with consistent precipitants. Her symptoms are three weeks old and the threshold has fallen from heavy exertion to one flight of stairs - one flight of stairs is the operational definition of CCS class III. That makes this new-onset angina of at least CCS III AND crescendo angina, two of the three accepted unstable-angina presentations, neither of which requires rest pain. Absence of rest pain is the commonest reasoning error on this case; it is not reassurance.

model_note.S:
cc: Chest pressure with exertion for 3 weeks

HPI: 30 yo f with a history of HTN, familial hypercholesterolemia and prediabetes presents to clinic c/o substernal chest pressure that started 3 weeks ago. Episodes are brought on by exertion - carrying boxes, climbing one flight of stairs - last about 5 minutes and resolve with rest. Pressure is described as a heaviness, 6/10 at worst, radiating to the left arm and intermittently to the jaw. Progressive: initially only with heavy exertion, now with less. Associated with exertional dyspnea, diaphoresis and mild nausea. Denies pain at rest, syncope, palpitations, orthopnea, PND and lower extremity edema. Not positional, not pleuritic, not related to meals. Antacids gave no relief. No prior similar episodes. Concerned this is her heart; her father died of an MI at 41.

PMH: HTN, familial hypercholesterolemia, prediabetes.
PSH: Appendectomy age 20. No hospitalizations since.
Meds: Lisinopril 20 mg 1 tab daily; atorvastatin 40 mg 1 tab nightly. Not on aspirin.
SH: Warehouse supervisor. Current smoker, 1 ppd x 12 years. 2-3 beers most evenings. Denies illicit drug use including cocaine. Sedentary, poor diet.
FH: Father died of MI at 41. Mother 55 with HTN and DM. Brother 32 with inherited high cholesterol.
Allergies: NKDA.
ROS: Cardiovascular - admits exertional chest pressure, dyspnea, diaphoresis; denies palpitations, syncope, orthopnea, edema. Respiratory - denies cough, hemoptysis and wheezing. GI - admits mild nausea; denies heartburn, vomiting and abdominal pain.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.
Reproductive history: My last period was 2 weeks ago.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.4 F oral, P 88 bpm, BP 158/94 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 97% on room air, Ht 5'9", Wt 205 lbs

General: Overweight young woman, comfortable at rest, in no acute distress. Alert and oriented.
Heart: RRR, S1 and S2 present with an S4 gallop, no murmurs or rubs. PMI non-displaced. No JVD at 30 degrees. Radial, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+ and symmetric, no carotid bruits.
Lungs: CTA bilaterally anterior and posterior. No rales, rhonchi or wheezes.
Chest wall: Non-tender to palpation; palpation does not reproduce the pain.
Abd: Bowel sounds present in 4 quadrants. Soft, non-tender including the epigastrium.
Exts: No lower extremity edema. No calf tenderness. Capillary refill under 2 seconds.
Osteopathic: T1-T5 left paraspinal tissue texture change, tenderness and restricted motion; T3 sidebent right, rotated right.
P: 1. Obtain a 12-lead ECG promptly and serial high-sensitivity troponin through the emergency team; assess current symptoms and vital signs, and arrange transfer to the emergency department now by EMS. Discuss aspirin only after allergy and bleeding review; anti-ischemic medicines require clinician review of blood pressure, possible severe aortic stenosis and relevant contraindications. Explain the worsening exertional pattern and why routine exercise stress testing is inappropriate before acute coronary syndrome is excluded.

2. Transthoracic echocardiogram of the heart with Doppler during this evaluation to measure aortic valve area, peak velocity and mean gradient and to assess left ventricular hypertrophy; cardiology to read it alongside the ischemic workup. No heavy exertion and no stair climbing until the valve is assessed. Educate that exertional chest pain, exertional shortness of breath and fainting are the three symptoms that change the prognosis of a stiff aortic valve, and that any near-faint means returning immediately.

3. Only after acute coronary syndrome is excluded: omeprazole 20 mg 1 tab daily 30 minutes before breakfast for an 8 week trial. Structured tobacco cessation with nicotine replacement, no food within 3 hours of lying down, and head of the bed elevated. OMT is deferred today; rib raising and paraspinal inhibition at T1-T5 may be offered once ischemia is excluded, because improvement after manual treatment cannot exclude ischemia. Educate that relief with an antacid or with OMT does not rule out heart disease.

ideal_encounter_extras: Ask explicitly whether she is on aspirin. It changes the plan and it is the kind of detail a differential-with-a-plan lives on.
Quantify the tobacco history in pack-years rather than 'she smokes' - the rubric asks for specific documentation.
Ask about cocaine by name in a chest pain case; 'do you use drugs' is easy to answer no to.
Palpate the chest wall deliberately and say what you are testing for. The value of this maneuver is the NEGATIVE, and a negative you can document is worth as much as a positive.
Ask what she thinks is going on before reassuring her. Her answer is the F.I.F.E. item, and it is also the reason she finally came in.

Abd: Bowel sounds present in 4 quadrants. Soft, non-tender including the epigastrium.
Exts: No lower extremity edema. No calf tenderness. Capillary refill under 2 seconds.
Osteopathic: T1-T5 left paraspinal tissue texture change, tenderness and restricted motion; T3 sidebent right, rotated right.
P: 1. Obtain a 12-lead ECG promptly and serial high-sensitivity troponin through the emergency team; assess current symptoms and vital signs, and arrange transfer to the emergency department now by EMS. Discuss aspirin only after allergy and bleeding review; anti-ischemic medicines require clinician review of blood pressure, possible severe aortic stenosis and relevant contraindications. Explain the worsening exertional pattern and why routine exercise stress testing is inappropriate before acute coronary syndrome is excluded. Use plain language, pause between steps, and invite teach-back.

2. Transthoracic echocardiogram of the heart with Doppler during this evaluation to measure aortic valve area, peak velocity and mean gradient and to assess left ventricular hypertrophy; cardiology to read it alongside the ischemic workup. No heavy exertion and no stair climbing until the valve is assessed. Educate that exertional chest pain, exertional shortness of breath and fainting are the three symptoms that change the prognosis of a stiff aortic valve, and that any near-faint means returning immediately.

3. Only after acute coronary syndrome is excluded: omeprazole 20 mg 1 tab daily 30 minutes before breakfast for an 8 week trial. Structured tobacco cessation with nicotine replacement, no food within 3 hours of lying down, and head of the bed elevated. OMT is deferred today; rib raising and paraspinal inhibition at T1-T5 may be offered once ischemia is excluded, because improvement after manual treatment cannot exclude ischemia. Educate that relief with an antacid or with OMT does not rule out heart disease.

model_note.S:
cc: Chest pressure with exertion for 3 weeks

HPI: 30 yo f with a history of HTN, familial hypercholesterolemia and prediabetes presents to clinic c/o substernal chest pressure that started 3 weeks ago. Episodes are brought on by exertion - carrying boxes, climbing one flight of stairs - last about 5 minutes and resolve with rest. Pressure is described as a heaviness, 6/10 at worst, radiating to the left arm and intermittently to the jaw. Progressive: initially only with heavy exertion, now with less. Associated with exertional dyspnea, diaphoresis and mild nausea. Denies pain at rest, syncope, palpitations, orthopnea, PND and lower extremity edema. Not positional, not pleuritic, not related to meals. Antacids gave no relief. No prior similar episodes. Concerned this is her heart; her father died of an MI at 41.

PMH: HTN, familial hypercholesterolemia, prediabetes.
PSH: Appendectomy age 20. No hospitalizations since.
Meds: Lisinopril 20 mg 1 tab daily; atorvastatin 40 mg 1 tab nightly. Not on aspirin.
SH: Warehouse supervisor. Current smoker, 1 ppd x 12 years. 2-3 beers most evenings. Denies illicit drug use including cocaine. Sedentary, poor diet.
FH: Father died of MI at 41. Mother 55 with HTN and DM. Brother 32 with inherited high cholesterol.
Allergies: NKDA.
ROS: Cardiovascular - admits exertional chest pressure, dyspnea, diaphoresis; denies palpitations, syncope, orthopnea, edema. Respiratory - denies cough, hemoptysis and wheezing. GI - admits mild nausea; denies heartburn, vomiting and abdominal pain.

Patient concern: I am worried about getting to follow-up and knowing whom to call if I get worse.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.
Reproductive history: My last period was 2 weeks ago.

Vitals: T 98.4 F oral, P 88 bpm, BP 158/94 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 97% on room air, Ht 5'9", Wt 205 lbs

General: Overweight young woman, comfortable at rest, in no acute distress. Alert and oriented.
Heart: RRR, S1 and S2 present with an S4 gallop, no murmurs or rubs. PMI non-displaced. No JVD at 30 degrees. Radial, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+ and symmetric, no carotid bruits.
Lungs: CTA bilaterally anterior and posterior. No rales, rhonchi or wheezes.
Chest wall: Non-tender to palpation; palpation does not reproduce the pain.
Abd: Bowel sounds present in 4 quadrants. Soft, non-tender including the epigastrium.
Exts: No lower extremity edema. No calf tenderness. Capillary refill under 2 seconds.
Osteopathic: T1-T5 left paraspinal tissue texture change, tenderness and restricted motion; T3 sidebent right, rotated right.
P: 1. Obtain a 12-lead ECG promptly and serial high-sensitivity troponin through the emergency team; assess current symptoms and vital signs, and arrange transfer to the emergency department now by EMS. Discuss aspirin only after allergy and bleeding review; anti-ischemic medicines require clinician review of blood pressure, possible severe aortic stenosis and relevant contraindications. Explain the worsening exertional pattern and why routine exercise stress testing is inappropriate before acute coronary syndrome is excluded. Agree on a practical contact and transportation plan; verify the patient can describe the urgent warning signs.

2. Transthoracic echocardiogram of the heart with Doppler during this evaluation to measure aortic valve area, peak velocity and mean gradient and to assess left ventricular hypertrophy; cardiology to read it alongside the ischemic workup. No heavy exertion and no stair climbing until the valve is assessed. Educate that exertional chest pain, exertional shortness of breath and fainting are the three symptoms that change the prognosis of a stiff aortic valve, and that any near-faint means returning immediately.

3. Only after acute coronary syndrome is excluded: omeprazole 20 mg 1 tab daily 30 minutes before breakfast for an 8 week trial. Structured tobacco cessation with nicotine replacement, no food within 3 hours of lying down, and head of the bed elevated. OMT is deferred today; rib raising and paraspinal inhibition at T1-T5 may be offered once ischemia is excluded, because improvement after manual treatment cannot exclude ischemia. Educate that relief with an antacid or with OMT does not rule out heart disease.
